efficacy.population: Unselected (adults with OIC on opioids for chronic non-cancer pain)
efficacy.confidence_note: Year is a proxy: axelopran entered phase 1 (NCT01040637) in January 2010, so the preclinical package predates it; model data first public in 2013. Abstract-level for Armstrong 2013 (paywalled).
efficacy.judgement: A different agonist (loperamide) and readout (gastric emptying) from the draft's rat morphine small-intestinal transit track, so its own track.
efficacy.quote: Oral administration of TD-1211, naltrexone, and ADL 08-0011 reversed loperamide-induced inhibition of gastric emptying and castor oil-induced diarrhea in rats and nonproductive GI circular smooth muscle contractility in dogs.
efficacy.note: Oral axelopran reversed loperamide-delayed gastric emptying and castor-oil diarrhoea in rats, predicting OIC relief.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: CSBM change vs placebo at week 5 (baseline 0.2 to almost 3 at 15 mg) against rat gastric-emptying ID50 0.24 mg/kg
efficacy.population: Unselected (adults with OIC on opioids for chronic non-cancer pain)
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text (PMC6912869). Patient results are the sponsor authors' summary of the axelopran phase 2b (NCT01459926, no registry results posted; presented ACG 2012 and as conference abstracts); no full peer-reviewed trial paper found.
efficacy.judgement: The paper states the rat loperamide gastric-emptying data and the phase 2b result side by side. Registry primary is CSBMs over weeks 2-5; the paper reports week 5, taken as the primary.
efficacy.quote: The key efficacy highlight from the most recent 200 OIC patient Phase 2b study revealed a statistically significant (p = 0.0001) increase in complete spontaneous bowel movements (CSBMs) relative to placebo
efficacy.note: Axelopran phase 2b raised CSBMs over placebo in 200 OIC patients, as the rat gastric-emptying model predicted.

safety.population: Unselected (adults with OIC on opioids for chronic non-cancer pain)
safety.confidence_note: Year is a proxy: axelopran entered phase 1 (NCT01040637) in January 2010, so the preclinical package predates it; model data first public in 2013. Abstract-level for Armstrong 2013 (paywalled).
safety.judgement: Mouse, not the draft's rat withdrawal model, so its own track.
safety.quote: Oral administration of naltrexone and ADL 08-0011, but not TD-1211 or alvimopan, was associated with a CNS withdrawal response in morphine-dependent mice, inhibition of morphine-induced anti-nociception in rat and dog hot plate tests, and hypothermia and sedation in dogs.
safety.note: Axelopran, unlike naltrexone, evoked no CNS withdrawal in morphine-dependent mice, predicting no central withdrawal in patients.
safety.short: No CNS withdrawal in dependent mice

safety.magnitude_basis: treatment-emergent adverse events vs placebo against absent CNS withdrawal at 30 mg/kg in mice
safety.population: Unselected (adults with OIC on opioids for chronic non-cancer pain)

safety.judgement: Patient side is a summary statement, not a withdrawal-scale result; scored same as the model's stated absence of central harm held, partial because withdrawal scales were not reported.
safety.quote: Axelopran (TD-1211) 19i has been well-tolerated across all studies with observation of similar treatment emergent adverse events relative to placebo.
safety.note: Axelopran was well tolerated across phase 1-2 with adverse events similar to placebo, matching the mice's lack of CNS withdrawal.
